Armed with only a trowel for stirring the earth and a tangle of twine to secure fragile plants, I navigate the sterilized earth under cracked glass, where forgotten trays of dry compost await their second chance.

My steps lead me north, across the threshold of the dormant furnace, its iron cold and memories long extinguished. Here, in this adjacency of death and potential life, a lone lantern catches my attention, a beacon amidst shadows and neglect. I seize the opportunity for light, for guidance in my endeavor.

Eastward, through a low archway, lies the fernery—a realm of verdant whispers and unfurling leaves waiting to breathe again under my care. With lantern in hand, I venture forth, ready to coax back to life what time has stilled.
